_comment: Site-specific configuration for the dropbox.com homepage replica.
The pipeline scripts are URL-agnostic; all site knowledge lives here.
_captureMode: Decided on a DOM-level probe, not the 'auto' element-count ratio.
Measured this run (scrape/probe-capture-source.mjs), static vs rendered:
elements 1519/1673 (0.908 - would have PASSED the 0.7 element test),
but video 0/4, iframe 0/3, svg 27/39, source 20/31, and the security
quote-cards grid div._quoteCardsGrid_thadj_158 ships 0 children vs 3.
A static build therefore silently loses all 4 product videos and the

_skipStylesheets: Dropbox links an UNCOMPILED SCSS source from <head> (// comments,
hard-fails with 'Unknown word'. Safe to skip only because the compiled
twin sheet redefines the same 15 @font-face rules / 75 url()s.
Filename hash is capture-bound - re-confirm it after each capture.
_dropSelectors: This key REPLACES the template defaults rather than merging, so the
defaults are repeated verbatim below, then 5 site-specific entries:
the CCPA consent banner, two marketing/blank iframes, the
.mov/hvc1 <source> siblings (the hero .mov alone is 134MB and no
harness browser ever selects it - the .webm siblings are what play),
and the empty mp4 fallback <source src=""> each of the 4 videos
carries. That last one is INERT in a browser (an empty src is never
selected) but React warns 'An empty string was passed to the src
attribute' once per video, which the viewport audit counts as 4
console errors - and console-errors has NO baseline path, so it has
to be removed rather than accepted. Dropping it changes no pixels;
the .webm sibling above it is what every browser actually plays.

_extraAssets: dropbox.com declares its favicon with the legacy two-token form
rel="shortcut icon". The template's ref matcher now handles that, so this
is belt-and-braces: pinned, explicit, and costs nothing. Without a local
copy the browser probes /favicon.ico at the origin root and logs a 404
that the viewport audit counts as a console error (no baseline path).
